title: Forensic Report & Identify The Null
instructions: Write the final forensic report and identify the operator behind the tournament incident.

briefing.narrative: All analysis is complete. The final step is to identify the operator behind the attack and produce a compliant forensic report. Review the suspect profiles and the report template before making your conclusions.
briefing.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Review the suspect profiles and report template

identify.narrative: The evidence points to a specific operator. Review the suspect profiles and select the individual whose handle was embedded in the malware memory.
identify.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Aberr4ti0n (Amorsolo de la Cruz) — the handle was found in the memory dump
choices.feedback: Correct. The handle 'Aberr4ti0n' was embedded in the C2 client process memory.

choices.text: Du11ahan (Carrie Ashworth) — the meticulous English operative
choices.feedback: No evidence links Du11ahan to this endpoint. The handle in memory is Aberr4ti0n.

report.narrative: Now produce the report. Review the NIST SP 800-86 template and choose the correct set of sections for a compliant forensic report.
report.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Include case summary, evidence acquisition, analysis, findings, and recommendations
choices.feedback: Correct. A complete forensic report covers all of these sections.

choices.text: Include only the suspect name and the conclusion
choices.feedback: A name and conclusion alone do not satisfy forensic reporting standards.

complete.narrative: The forensic report has been submitted. The operator is identified as Aberr4ti0n. The case is now ready for law enforcement and the tournament incident response team.
complete.speaker: instructor

items.title: NIST SP 800-86 report template
items.description: Sections required for a compliant forensic report.
items.content:
Forensic Report Template (NIST SP 800-86)

1. Case Summary
   - Incident reference number, date/time, and scope

2. Evidence Acquisition
   - Items collected, collection method, hash values, chain of custody

3. Analysis
   - Tools and techniques used
   - Evidence processed (laptop, memory, network)
   - Timeline of activity

4. Findings
   - Observable facts and their significance
   - Identified suspect or root cause
   - Indicators of compromise

5. Conclusions and Recommendations
   - Summary of impact
   - Remediation steps
   - Suggested controls to prevent recurrence

6. Appendices
   - Raw evidence references, hash logs, tool outputs
